Anne, whether as the gay little orphan in her conquest of the master and mistress of Green Gables, or as the maturing and self-forgetful maiden of Avonlea, keeps up to concert-pitch in her charm and her winsomeness. There is nothing in her to disappoint hope or imagination.

arxiv-2110-05019.title: Novel triple barrier potential for axial gravitational perturbations of a family of Lorentzian wormholes
arxiv-2110-05019.creator: Poulami Dutta Roy
arxiv-2110-05019.description: Abstract We study the behavior of a specific Lorentzian wormhole family under gravitational perturbations. In earlier work [EPJC 80, 850 (2020)], we have proved the stability of a test scalar field in the background of the wormhole family, where the effective potential was that of a double barrier.

arxiv-2305-09046.title: Optimization Over a Probability Simplex
arxiv-2305-09046.creator: James Chok james.chok@ed.ac.uk, Geoffrey M. Vasil gvasil@ed.ac.uk
arxiv-2305-09046.description: Abstract We propose a new iteration scheme, the Cauchy-Simplex, to optimize convex problems over the probability simplex { w ∈ ℝ n | ∑ i w i = 1 ​ and ​ w i ≥ 0 } \{w\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\ |\ \sum_{i}w_{i}=1\ \textrm{and}\ w_{i}\geq 0\} .

arxiv-2312-00742.title: Scalable Meta-Learning with Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2312-00742.creator: Petru Tighineanu, Lukas Grossberger, Paul Baireuther, Kathrin Skubch, Stefan Falkner, Julia Vinogradska, Felix Berkenkamp
arxiv-2312-00742.description: Abstract Meta-learning is a powerful approach that exploits historical data to quickly solve new tasks from the same distribution. In the low-data regime, methods based on the closed-form posterior of Gaussian processes (GP) together with Bayesian optimization have achieved high performance.

arxiv-2312-07664.title: Orbital Torus Imaging: Acceleration, density, and dark matter in the Galactic disk measured with element abundance gradients Agama ( Vasiliev 2019 ) , Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , gala ( Price-Whelan 2017b ) ,
arxiv-2312-07664.creator: Danny Horta, Adrian M. Price-Whelan, David W. Hogg, Kathryn V. Johnston, Lawrence Widrow, Julianne J. Dalcanton, Melissa K. Ness, Jason A. S. Hunt
arxiv-2312-07664.description: Abstract Under the assumption of a simple and time-invariant gravitational potential, many Galactic dynamics techniques infer the Milky Way’s mass and dark matter distribution from stellar kinematic observations. These methods typically rely on parameterized potential models of the Galaxy and must take into account non-trivial survey selection effects, because they make use of the density of stars in phase space.

arxiv-2401-12438.description: Abstract . The recent pandemic has delivered a desire for understanding COVID-19 diagnoses among patients in hospitals. Currently, hospitals have difficulty diagnosing this novel respiratory illness from a patient’s chest X-Ray to another, simply because it is difficult to compare COVID chest X-Ray between patients due to HIPAA compliance.

arxiv-2412-04082.title: Learnable Similarity and Dissimilarity Guided Symmetric Non-Negative Matrix Factorization
arxiv-2412-04082.creator: Wenlong Lyu, Yuheng Jia
arxiv-2412-04082.description: Abstract Symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization (SymNMF) is a powerful tool for clustering, which typically uses the k k -nearest neighbor ( k k -NN) method to construct similarity matrix. However, k k -NN may mislead clustering since the neighbors may belong to different clusters, and its reliability generally decreases as k k grows.

arxiv-2502-08602.title: Stretching Response of a Polymer Chain with Deformable Bonds
arxiv-2502-08602.creator: Jie Zhu, Laurence Brassart
arxiv-2502-08602.description: Abstract The stretching response of polymer chains fundamentally determines the mechanical properties of polymer networks. In this Letter, we develop a statistical mechanics model that incorporates both bond stretching and bond angle deformation, enabling accurate predictions of chain behavior up to large forces.

arxiv-2511-22123.title: Model Predictive Path Planning in Navier–Stokes Flow with POD-Based Reduced-Order Models
arxiv-2511-22123.creator: Adam Waterman, Martin Guay
arxiv-2511-22123.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Adam Waterman, Martin Guay. We present a framework for optimal trajectory generation in flow-driven systems governed by the Navier–Stokes equations, combining a Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) reduced-order model (ROM) with Model Predictive Control (MPC). The approach (i) approximates the velocity field from data via snapshot POD and orthogonal projection, (ii) derives a Galerkin-projected dynamical model in reduced coordinates, and (iii) employs MPC to plan control inputs that steer an agent through the predicted flow while satisfying state and actuation constraints.

pmc-10628182.title: Corvids optimize working memory by categorizing continuous stimuli
pmc-10628182.creator: Aylin Apostel, Matthew Panichello, Timothy J Buschman, Jonas Rose
pmc-10628182.description: Working memory (WM) is a crucial element of the higher cognition of primates and corvid songbirds. Despite its importance, WM has a severely limited capacity and is vulnerable to noise. In primates, attractor dynamics mitigate the effect of noise by discretizing continuous information. Yet, it remains unclear whether similar dynamics are seen in avian brains.

pmc-11304191.title: Healthcare workers’ knowledge of indicators for a palliative care approach
pmc-11304191.creator: Jennie Morgan, Ruth Amoore, Sadiya Z. Patel, Katya Evans, Rene Krause
pmc-11304191.description: BackgroundPalliative care is an essential element of universal healthcare, yet not all people who need palliative care are able to receive it. One of the barriers to ensuring access for people who require palliative care is the identification of those eligible.

pmc-12608595.title: Long Noncoding RNA Lnc-MTPAP-1 Overexpressed by Particulate Matter Suppresses Apoptosis in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) Cells
pmc-12608595.creator: Ji Won Park, Daeun Kang, Min Hyeok Lee, Yeonwoo Lee, Su Yel Lee, Sin Yung Woo, Keum-Jin Yang, In Beom Jeong, Hee Sun Park, Ji Woong Son, Sun Jung Kwon
pmc-12608595.description: Lung cancer remains one of the most common and lethal malignancies worldwide, with poor prognosis largely due to late-stage diagnosis and resistance to therapy. Emerging evidence indicates that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play critical roles in cancer development, metastasis, and treatment resistance.

pmc-12750135.title: Systemic Autoimmune Rheumatic Disease Risk: Association With Long‐Term Exposure to Fine Particulate Matter
pmc-12750135.creator: Mareva Geslin, Julien Vachon, Naizhuo Zhao, Elhadji Anassour Laouan Sidi, Sonia Jean, Audrey Smargiassi, Sasha Bernatsky
pmc-12750135.description: ObjectiveFine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a possible trigger of systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). We investigated SARDs risk related to long‐term exposure to PM2.5 and its components (ammonium, black carbon, mineral dust, sea salt, nitrate, sulfate, organic matter), the composition of which may affect toxicity.

pmc-13021409.creator: Ganzhen Ding, Wenbo Wang, Weidong Tao
pmc-13021409.description: IntroductionAlthough previous research has linked growth mindset to the intrapersonal dimensions of social emotional skills, little is known about how different mindset types relate to these skills. Moreover, the role of negative automatic thoughts in this relationship among Grade 5 and Grade 6 elementary students remains unclear.

pmc-13096506.title: Counterproductive: coinfection of a water flea by a fungus and a microsporidium reduces the reproductive outputs of all parties
pmc-13096506.creator: Snir Halle, Aran Sofer, Frida Ben-Ami
pmc-13096506.description: Organisms are often coinfected by more than one parasite species. These coinfections can alter the fitness of both host and its coinfecting parasites. Changes in host fitness are usually estimated by comparing parasite virulence under coinfection to the virulence of each parasite under single infection.

pmc-13453350.title: Application Prospects of Nanotechnology in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Diseases
pmc-13453350.creator: Zailian Zhou, Jingjing Cui, Yecong Tang, Junlin Wang, Huizhi Mu, Guangzhe Li, Kun Shao, Xuejian Wang, Zhenzhu Liu
pmc-13453350.description: Cardiovascular diseases pose significant threats to human health due to their high incidence and mortality rates; therefore, early diagnosis, precise treatment, and improvement of long-term prognosis remain key research priorities in this field. Traditional diagnostic methods for cardiovascular diseases primarily rely on echocardiography, contrast-enhanced CT, or MRI, which exhibit low sensitivity and specificity, poor image clarity, and radiation exposure.

pmc-13488347.title: SH3PXD2B is the critical host factor promoting the entry of mycobacteria
pmc-13488347.creator: Donghui Liu, Ting Zhang, Yujie Sheng, Zhengzhong Xu, Chengkun Zheng, Yingyu Chen, Aizhen Guo, Xin'an Jiao, Xiang Chen
pmc-13488347.description: Bovine tuberculosis (bTB), caused by Mycobacterium bovis, causes major economic losses in the global livestock industry and threatens public health. Macrophages are essential for pathogen clearance, yet serve as the primary intracellular niche for mycobacterial survival. These characteristics emphasize the importance of identifying host factors that regulate macrophage functions during infection.

pmc-13626781.title: Integrated care management and comprehensive geriatric assessment using a mHealth-based approach in older multimorbid patients with atrial fibrillation: the AFFIRMO cluster-randomised trial
pmc-13626781.creator: Gregory Y.H. Lip, Marco Proietti, John Ainsworth, Gheorghe-Andrei Dan, Lars Frost, Guendalina Graffigna, Deirdre A. Lane, Donata Lucci, Gianna Fabbri, Francisco Marin, Martin O'Flaherty, Mirko Petrovic, Tatjana S. Potpara, Riccardo Proietti, Alam Sanaullah, Mariya Tokmakova, Davide Liborio Vetrano,
pmc-13626781.description: SummaryBackgroundThe AFFIRMO trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a mobile-health (mHealth) structured intervention adapting the Atrial Fibrillation Better Care (ABC) pathway, combining the comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), to enhance guideline-directed, holistic AF management and reduce the risk of clinical outcomes in older patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and multimorbidity.

pmc-13649081.title: Cardiac magnetic resonance T1 mapping predicts outcome in patients with a systemic right ventricle: a sub-analysis of the SERVE study
pmc-13649081.creator: Odile Burdet, Kerstin Wustmann, Barbara E U Burkhardt, Emanuela R Valsangiacomo Buechel, Jean-Paul Vallée, Judith Bouchardy, Matthias Greutmann, Markus Schwerzmann, Harald Gabriel, Dominik Stambach, Daniel Tobler, Juerg Schwitter, Tobias Rutz, Annette Schophuus Jensen
pmc-13649081.description: AimsIn patients with a systemic right ventricle (sRV), the sRV is faced with an increased afterload compared to a right ventricle in sub-pulmonary position, leading to the development of fibrosis followed by ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) T1 mapping (T1) and its derived parameter, such as the extracellular volume (ECV), allow quantification of interstitial fibrosis.
